tagline: Up the quiet side of the Tetons to seed potato country.
intro: Out of Swan Valley, Idaho 31 goes northeast as Pine Creek Road, crossing Rainey Creek and Pine Creek and running through the mountains of the Targhee National Forest, south of Stouts Mountain, before it comes into Victor. There the byway turns north up Teton Valley on Idaho 33, through Driggs and Tetonia, and takes Idaho 32 across the open fields to Ashton.

Union Pacific ran its Teton Valley Branch from Ashton to Driggs and Victor in 1912, and the Ashton-Tetonia Trail now follows an old Union Pacific spur. At the north end the long, killing freeze of an Ashton winter clears the soil of potato blight, and the town bills itself as the world's largest seed potato growing area.

moments.title: Victor
moments.text: Four settlements became one town here in 1889, named for George Victor Sherwood, a mail carrier who kept delivering the mail despite threats of attack.

moments.title: Driggs
moments.text: The county seat stands in the valley the fur trade called Pierre's Hole, where trappers, traders and tribes gathered for the rendezvous of 1832.

moments.title: Ashton
moments.text: The first American Dog Derby ran 55 miles down the unplowed rail line from West Yellowstone to Ashton in 1917, and a blizzard kept the crowd waiting two days for the finish.
